title: How to add a breakpoint in Xcode on Mac: expert guide for developers
metaTitle: How to add a breakpoint in Xcode on Mac: Quick Steps
description: Learn how to add a breakpoint in Xcode on Mac to debug your applications. Follow these simple steps to pause code execution and inspect your variables.
targetKeyword: how to add a breakpoint in xcode on mac
intro: To add a breakpoint in Xcode on Mac, click the gutter area to the left of your line numbers in the source editor. You can also place your cursor on any line and press Command plus Backslash to toggle a breakpoint instantly.
tldr: Click the gutter to set a breakpoint.
Use Command + 7 to open the Breakpoint navigator.

blocks.text: Breakpoints are the most effective way to debug logic errors in your code. Instead of adding print statements and rebuilding your entire project, a breakpoint pauses the application at a specific moment. This lets you inspect the state of your variables, the call stack, and the flow of your logic in real time. It saves significant time during daily development cycles.

The most common way to add a breakpoint in Xcode is the gutter method. The gutter is the vertical strip on the left side of your code editor. When you click it, a blue marker appears. This marker tells the debugger to stop execution as soon as that line of code is reached. You can disable the breakpoint by clicking the marker, which turns it grey. To delete it, drag the marker away from the gutter until it disappears.

Efficiency matters when you are deep in a coding session. You do not need to reach for your mouse to set a breakpoint. Place your cursor on the line where you want to pause execution. Press Command + Backslash on your keyboard. This toggles the breakpoint on or off. It is a fast way to manage your debugging flow without breaking your focus.

Sometimes you only want to stop execution when a specific condition is met. Control-click on your blue breakpoint marker in the gutter. Choose Edit Breakpoint from the menu. You can enter a condition like i == 10. The debugger will only pause if that condition evaluates to true. You can also add actions. These actions can log a message to the console or run a debugger command. You can even check the box to automatically continue after the action runs. This is useful for logging values without interrupting your app flow.

As your project grows, you might end up with dozens of breakpoints scattered across many files. The Breakpoint navigator helps you keep track of them. Press Command + 7 to open the navigator sidebar. You will see a list of every breakpoint in your project. You can enable or disable them in bulk by clicking the checkboxes. You can also add new types of breakpoints here, such as Symbolic or Exception breakpoints, by clicking the plus button at the bottom of the pane.

If your breakpoint is not hitting, check your build scheme first. Debugging usually requires the Debug scheme. If you are running a Release build, the compiler might optimize the code and remove the line entirely. Another common fix is to clean your build folder. Press Shift + Command + K to perform a clean build. This often resolves weird issues where the debugger and your source code are out of sync.

faq.question: Why is my breakpoint not working in Xcode?
faq.answer: Ensure you are using the Debug build scheme. If you are using Release, compiler optimizations may skip your code. Try cleaning the build folder with Shift + Command + K.

faq.question: Can I add a breakpoint on a specific part of a line?
faq.answer: Yes. If a line has multiple expressions, Control-click the specific part of the code and choose Create Column Breakpoint.

faq.question: How do I see all my breakpoints?
faq.answer: Press Command + 7 to open the Breakpoint navigator in the left sidebar.

steps.name: Click the gutter
steps.text: Locate the gutter to the left of your code line numbers in the editor. Click once to place a blue breakpoint marker.
steps.tip: Click the blue marker again to disable it.

steps.name: Use the shortcut
steps.text: Place your cursor on the line of code. Press Command + Backslash to toggle the breakpoint.

steps.name: Open the navigator
steps.text: Use the shortcut to view all active breakpoints in your project.

troubleshooting.fix: Check that you are using the Debug scheme and perform a clean build.

troubleshooting.fix: Verify the symbol name for typos.
